name: Yamaha TX81Z
source: Yamaha TX81Z Owner's Manual (English, Patchman Music authorized scan TX81z_E-UM_HiQ.pdf, text layer read): pp.11-37 (store, edit, utility, Memory Protect p.27, Combine p.27, P.Change/Exclusive p.25-26, preset list p.4), pp.65-78 MIDI reception, 'SYSTEM EXCLUSIVE DATA FORMAT' (parameter change, bulk data, dump request, VCED/ACED/PCED/remote switch tables, VMEM/ACED/effect/PMEM/microtune/PC table/system bulk charts), specifications (480 x 282 x 45.2 mm). Cross-checked against Edisyn (github.com/eclab/edisyn, edisyn/synth/yamaha4op/Yamaha4Op.java: VCED/ACED/ACED2/ACED3/EFEDS param tables, VMEM pack/unpack, requests, 'TX81Z works'), Matt Gregory's TX81Z Programmer (github.com/mgregory22/tx81z-programmer: tx81z.h param/remote constants, tx81z_meta.c request strings + dump headers, txpack.c VMEM<->VCED/ACED and PMEM<->PCED bit maps, tx81z.c param-change framing, memory-protect handling, store-by-remote-switch, pacing, freqratios.c 64x16 ratio table) and KnobKraft-orm adaptations/Yamaha_TX81Z.py (v1.0 ACED checksum bug). Validated against the four factory voice banks A-D as real 4104-byte VMEM dumps (4OPHQ TX81Z_Presets.zip, tx81z_1..4.syx, via web.archive.org) and two real single-voice ACED+VCED dumps (the-all.org/tx81z/patches HollowBass.syx, Filter1.syx).

yamaha4op.channelNibble: Every TX81Z SysEx carries the MIDI channel in the low nibble of byte 2: n = channel - 1. Received messages must match UTILITY > Midi Control > Receive Ch (the 'basic receive channel', which also receives program changes and plays in SINGLE mode); dumps the unit sends carry its Transmit Ch. There is no separate device number. Set both to the editor channel and match replies on any n.

paramChange.groupByteNote: ggggg = 4 for every voice/performance message; hh = subgroup: 0x12 = VCED (hh 2), 0x13 = ACED (hh 3), 0x13 = remote switch (pp 64-75, shares ACED's byte), 0x10 = PCED (hh 0). The manual prints PCED as hh = 11 (3); Edisyn and TX81Z Programmer both found it is 0x10 on the hardware.
paramChange.voice: p.block 'VCED' -> F0 43 1n 12 <p.pp> <value> F7; p.block 'ACED' -> F0 43 1n 13 <p.pp> <value> F7. The value is the plain parameter value (no packing, no offset); pp = the param's position in the VCED (0-92) / ACED (0-22) dump data.
paramChange.opEnable: F0 43 1n 12 5D <0-15> F7 (VCED pp 93): bit3 OP1, bit2 OP2, bit1 OP3, bit0 OP4, 1 = on. Not in any dump; resets to all-on when a voice is selected.
paramChange.system: F0 43 1n 10 7B <kk> <dd> F7, kk = system index (chart 'System Setup Bulk Data': 0 master tune 0-172, 1 receive ch 0-15/16 omni, 2 transmit ch, 3 P.Change 0 off/1 com/2 ind, 4 Cont.Change 0 off/1 norm/2-17 G1-16, 5 Pitch Bend same, 6 note on/off 0 all/1 odd/2 even, 7 Exclusive 0/1, 8 Memory Protect 0 off/1 on, 9 Combine 0/1, 10 AT->BC 0/1). Puts the unit in UTILITY mode.
paramChange.effect: F0 43 1n 10 7C <kk> <dd> F7 (effect data index 0-54: delay/pan/chord). Puts the unit in UTILITY mode.
paramChange.programChangeTable: F0 43 1n 10 7F <pgm 0-127> <memHi 0-1> <memLo 0-127> F7, mem = 0-31 I01-I32, 32-63 A, 64-95 B, 96-127 C, 128-159 D, 160-183 PF01-PF24. Puts the unit in UTILITY mode.

remoteSwitch.note: Labels from the manual; TX81Z Programmer names 73/74 cursor left/right (they are cursor keys when the CURSOR LED is on). A click = press then release.

bulk.checksum: 7-bit two's complement of the sum of every data byte = (128 - sum % 128) % 128, where the data is everything after the two byte-count bytes up to the checksum, INCLUDING the 10-char 'LM  ....' header of 7E-type dumps. Verified on the 4 factory VMEM banks and on real ACED+VCED singles.
bulk.byteCount: 2 bytes, 7 bits each (hi, lo) = number of data bytes (incl. the 'LM  ....' header). The manual prints the VMEM count as '10 00' (hex of 4096); the wire bytes are 20 00 (verified on factory dumps; Edisyn notes the same).

VCED.data: VCED parameters 0-92 in parameter-number order (87-92 = DX21 pitch EG, unused: hold 99 99 99 50 50 50)

VMEM.data: 32 voices x 128 bytes, packed (see vmemLayout); internal bank I only

PCED.data: performance edit buffer, PCED params 0-109 unpacked

PMEM.data: 24 internal performances + 8 'initial' performances, 76 bytes each, packed (manual chart p.76)

SYS.data: system setup (27 bytes; firmware 1.0 sends 26 = 44-byte message without the AT byte)

MICROTUNE_FULL.note: manual misprints the count as 00 22; 266 data bytes = 02 0A

bulk.vmemLayout: Per voice 128 bytes. Operators stored OP4 (0-9), OP2 (10-19), OP3 (20-29), OP1 (30-39): +0 AR, +1 D1R, +2 D2R, +3 RR, +4 D1L, +5 LS, +6 AME(b6) EBS(b5-3) KVS(b2-0), +7 OUT, +8 CRS(b5-0), +9 RS(b4-3) DET(b2-0). 40 SY(b6) FB(b5-3) ALG(b2-0); 41 LFS; 42 LFD; 43 PMD; 44 AMD; 45 PMS(b6-4) AMS(b3-2) LFW(b1-0); 46 TRPS; 47 PBR; 48 CH(b4) MO(b3) SU(b2) PO(b1) PM(b0); 49 PORT; 50 FC VOL; 51 MW P; 52 MW A; 53 BC P; 54 BC A; 55 BC P BIAS; 56 BC E BIAS; 57-66 name; 67-72 DX21 pitch EG (set 99 99 99 50 50 50); 73+2k EGSFT(b5-4) FIX(b3) FIXRG(b2-0) and 74+2k OSW(b6-4) FINE(b3-0) for k = OP4, OP2, OP3, OP1; 81 REV(b2-0); 82 FC PITCH; 83 FC AMP; 84-127 zero on the TX81Z. Each param's 'vmem' {offset, shift, width} encodes this.

dumpRequest.editBufferVoice: F0 43 2n 7E 4C 4D 20 20 38 39 37 36 41 45 F7  ('LM  8976AE') -> ACED (41 bytes) then VCED (101 bytes)
dumpRequest.bankI: F0 43 2n 04 F7 -> VMEM (4104 bytes) of internal bank I; there is no request for preset banks A-D
dumpRequest.system: F0 43 2n 7E 'LM  8976S0' F7 (S1 = PC table, S2 = effects)
dumpRequest.note: No checksum or count in requests. n must equal the Receive Ch. Requests are ignored while Exclusive is off.

yamaha4op.editBufferSend: Send ACED first, then VCED: 'If ACED is received alone the VCED edit buffer is unaffected; if VCED is received alone the ACED edit buffer is initialized.' Received in PLAY/EDIT, not while the unit sits in UTILITY (TX81Z Programmer). Accepted with Memory Protect on (it only guards internal memory).
yamaha4op.memoryProtect: Memory Protect ON blocks STORE and the reception of VMEM (32 voices) and PMEM (24 performances). It is set ON at every power-up AND after every bulk receive (manual p.27), so turn it off (system param 8 = 0, then a PLAY click to leave UTILITY) immediately before each bank write.
yamaha4op.store: There is no 'store voice n' SysEx. Two paths: (a) documented: read-modify-write the whole bank I as VMEM (request VMEM, replace one 128-byte slot, memory protect off, send 4104 bytes); (b) remote-switch macro used by TX81Z Programmer: protect off, PLAY, select the target slot (program change), resend ACED+VCED, STORE press, DATA +1 click, STORE release, DATA +1 (YES) click. (b) depends on the unit's LCD state; (a) is deterministic and verifiable by reading VMEM back.
yamaha4op.programChange: Program changes go through the 128-entry Program Change Table (needs UTILITY P.Change = com). After 'Init P.Ch.Tbl' PC 0-127 = I01-C32; D01-D32 and PF01-24 are reachable only through table entries. Robust select (Edisyn): write table entry PGM128 = target mem (F0 43 1n 10 7F 7F hi lo F7), click PLAY (the table write left the unit in UTILITY), then Cn 7F. That permanently re-points PGM128 (default C32).

pacing.note: From TX81Z Programmer (70 ms default; 250 ms after OP level scaling, PCED voice number and effect pan range; 800 ms after a >4000-byte dump; 400 ms after >2000 bytes). Edisyn uses 50 ms per param and 100 ms after a patch change ('TX81Z fails if it's less than 50 or so'). The TX81Z is famously slow; faster bursts give 'MIDI Buffer Full'.

freqTables.ratioNote: freqTables.ratio[crs][fine] = the ratio the LCD shows in ratio mode (TX81Z Programmer freqratios.c; fine 0 and fine-max columns checked against Edisyn FREQUENCY_RATIOS / FREQUENCY_RATIOS_MAX). null = invalid (crs 0-3 accept fine 0-7 only).
freqTables.fixedHz: (((crs & 0x3C) << 2) + fine + (crs < 4 ? 8 : 0)) << fixRange  (TX81Z Programmer VoiceDlg_FixedParamsToFreq); range 0 = 8-255 Hz in 1 Hz steps ... range 7 = 1024-32640 Hz in 128 Hz steps (manual p.17 table).

waveNote: Operator waveforms W1-W8 (manual p.18, harmonic content p.50). W1 is a sine; W2-W8 are the YM2414's shaped/rectified/half-period variants. Labels kept as the LCD names (W1-W8).

banks.label: voices I (internal)
banks.note: Read: one VMEM request returns all 32 (cache it). Write: VMEM read-modify-write with Memory Protect off (see yamaha4op.store).

banks.label: voices A (preset)
banks.note: ROM. No dump request exists: select it, then request the edit buffer (ACED+VCED). (UTILITY 'Voice Transmit' can send A-D as VMEM but only from the panel or a remote-switch macro.)

banks.label: voices D (preset)
banks.note: ROM. Not reachable by the initialised PC table (PGM1-128 = I01-C32): needs the table-entry select.

banks.label: performances PF
banks.note: 8-part multitimbral setups. PMEM = 24 performances + 8 initial ones; raw backup/restore only (restore needs Memory Protect off). Performances reference voices by number (I01-D32), so restore voices first. Edit buffer = PCED.

programs.note: No bank select CCs. programChange(bank, prog): mem = bank.select.memBase + prog. If mem < 128 and the table is initialised, Cn <mem> works; otherwise (and always for D/PF) set PC-table entry 127 to mem, click PLAY, send Cn 7F. Selecting a voice in PLAY SINGLE loads it into the edit buffer (edits are lost; UTILITY 'Recall Edit' restores) and, with Exclusive on, the unit transmits that voice's ACED+VCED.

backup.restore: Send each dump back unchanged, >= 800 ms after VMEM and >= 400 ms after PMEM. Turn Memory Protect off before EACH of VMEM and PMEM (it switches back on after every bulk receive). Voices before performances. A received SYS dump also overwrites Receive/Transmit Ch, Exclusive and Memory Protect.

setup: Firmware: the startup screen shows the version. v1.0 has an ACED checksum bug (ACED sent to it shows an error and its extra params are not applied; VCED part is fine) and sends a 44-byte system dump; later versions (1.1-1.6) are fine.
[UTILITY] > Midi Control? YES > Receive Ch = the editor channel (SysEx and program changes are received on it; 'omn' also works).
Same page: Transmit Ch = the same channel (dumps come back on it).
Same page: Exclusive = on (off = no SysEx in or out). P. Change = com (common) so program changes use the Program Change Table.
[UTILITY] > Init P. Ch. Tbl. = YES (PC 1-128 = I01-C32), unless the user relies on a custom table; the editor re-points PGM 128 to reach D01-D32 and PF01-24.
[UTILITY] > Memory Protect = off before storing (it is ON after every power-up and after every bulk receive; the editor can switch it off over SysEx each time).
[UTILITY] > Combine = on (power-up default) so each voice's function data (bend range, porta, MW/BC/FC) is used.
Be in PLAY SINGLE mode (press PLAY/PERFORM until the voice name shows). Dumps are not received while the unit sits in UTILITY.
Cable both ways: interface out -> TX81Z MIDI IN, TX81Z MIDI OUT -> interface in.
driverNotes: Needs a NEW transport 'yamaha4op'; yamahaDriver cannot be reused by schema switches alone. Why: (1) yamahaDriver hard-codes the AWM2 'LM  8103' header + 26-byte header layout, 14-bit 11-byte param changes (F0 43 1n 35 G S H P V1 V2 F7) and a 521-byte element image; the TX81Z uses 7-byte param changes F0 43 1n <12|13|10> pp dd F7 with three different group bytes. (2) One voice is TWO messages (ACED 7E/'LM  8976AE' then VCED 03), with different headers, and the request returns both. (3) Stored voices exist only inside the packed 32-voice VMEM (bit fields, op order 4-2-3-1), there is no per-slot request, and storing needs memory-protect handling. (4) The channel nibble is the MIDI receive channel, not a device number. (5) Program change goes through a remappable table. Shared helpers worth factoring: checksum (same 7-bit two's complement), fetch-with-timeout. Driver sketch: sendParam(p,v): if p.bits -> keep a local opEnable byte (start 0x0F, reset to 0x0F after any program change or patch load), set bit, send F0 43 1n 12 5D <byte> F7; else F0 43 1n (p.block === 'ACED' ? 0x13 : 0x12) p.pp v F7; n = channel-1; pace 70 ms (250 ms after op*Ls). sendPatch(values): build vced[93] (87-92 = 99 99 99 50 50 50) and aced[23] from params (data index = p.pp), send ACED message then VCED message (checksums incl. 'LM  8976AE'), 70 ms apart. requestPatch(): send the 'LM  8976AE' request, collect the next ACED (41 bytes) and VCED (101 bytes) from F0 43 0x (any x), verify count+checksum (on firmware 1.0 tolerate a bad ACED checksum: keep VCED, flag ACED), decode values[p.key] = data[p.pp]; return {values, syx: aced+vced}. probe(): VCED-only request F0 43 2n 03 F7 within 900 ms; if silent, sweep n 0-15 once and remember the channel that answers. programChange(bi, prog): mem = bank.select.memBase + prog; if mem < 128 and prefs say the table is initialised send Cn mem; else send F0 43 1n 10 7F 7F (mem>>7) (mem&7F) F7, wait 70 ms, PLAY click (F0 43 1n 13 44 7F F7, F0 43 1n 13 44 00 F7), wait 70 ms, Cn 7F; then wait 100 ms and swallow (or adopt) the spontaneous ACED+VCED the unit sends for the new voice. requestBank(I): F0 43 2n 04 F7, wait up to ~3 s for 4104 bytes, verify, slice 32 x 128, decode each slot via p.vmem {offset, shift, width} (value = (byte >> shift) & ((1<<width)-1)); name = bytes 57-66; cache a few seconds (raw dump on slot 0 for backups). requestProgram(I, prog) = requestBank slot; for A-D (loadable, dump false) the editor selects + requestPatch. requestSlotName via the bank cache. writeProgram(I, prog, values): take the cached/fresh VMEM, rebuild slot prog by clearing then OR-ing every param's bits (keep bytes 67-72 and unknown bits from the read), send memory-protect-off F0 43 1n 10 7B 08 00 F7, wait 70 ms, PLAY click, wait 100 ms, send F0 43 0n 04 20 00 <4096> <sum> F7, wait >= 800 ms, re-request VMEM and compare (sameProgram on modelled fields). PMEM/system/effects/PC table/microtune: raw backup only. decode(ev): the TX81Z does not transmit parameter changes for panel edits; with Exclusive on it transmits ACED+VCED whenever a voice is selected in PLAY SINGLE (panel or PC) and PCED in PERFORMANCE: decode an unsolicited ACED+VCED pair into all voice values (ignore while our own request is in flight). Parameter changes put the unit in SINGLE EDIT; system/effect/PC-table changes put it in UTILITY (send PLAY to leave). Expect 'MIDI Buffer Full' on the LCD when changing patches (harmless; a key press clears it).
uncertain: Operator order in VCED/ACED parameter numbers: the manual's VCED and ACED tables label the 13/5-param blocks OP4, OP3, OP2, OP1, but its VMEM chart orders them OP4, OP2, OP3, OP1, and both hardware-tested editors (Edisyn, TX81Z Programmer) use OP4, OP2, OP3, OP1 for parameter changes and dumps. Schema follows the editors (supported by factory data: EG shift, 'fixed off' for OP1, is 0 in the OP1 slot of all 128 presets). Confirm: send F0 43 10 12 17 00 F7 (should silence OP2 OUT on the OP edit page).
PCED parameter-change group byte: manual says hh = 11 (0x13), both editors use 0x10; schema uses 0x10 (performance params are not modelled anyway).
Op enable bit order (VCED pp 93): manual only says 'Operator 4-1 On/Off (bits 0-3)'; bit3 = OP1 ... bit0 = OP4 is from TX81Z Programmer's checkbox wiring. Untested here.

Remote switches 67, 73, 74: manual = EDIT, MASTER VOLUME -1/+1; TX81Z Programmer = COMPARE, CURSOR left/right (same physical keys, mode-dependent). Only 65 STORE, 68 PLAY and 72 DATA+1 are needed by the store/select macros.

Whether a voice selected by a MIDI program change (not the panel) also triggers the spontaneous ACED+VCED transmission: the manual says 'when a voice is selected while in PLAY SINGLE mode'; drivers should request the edit buffer anyway.

Whether VMEM is received while the unit is in SINGLE EDIT (vs PLAY) and whether a VMEM write reloads the voice now playing: not documented. The macro clicks PLAY first; re-request the edit buffer after a bank write.

Store by remote-switch macro (TX81Z Programmer): sequence STORE press, DATA+1, STORE release, DATA+1 implies the target is pre-selected by the program change; depends on LCD state and was not tested here. The VMEM read-modify-write path is the recommended one.

Fixed-frequency formula and the 64x16 ratio table come from TX81Z Programmer (the manual gives only ranges and step sizes). They agree with the manual's ranges (8-255 Hz ... 1024-32640 Hz) and with Edisyn's per-coarse min/max ratios except one cell: crs 2 fine 7 = 1.47 (TX81Z Programmer, fits that row's ~0.098 step) vs Edisyn max 1.37 (looks like a typo). Kept 1.47.
Waveforms W2-W8 have no official names; labelled W1 sine, W2-W8.
Detune magnitude (manual: about +/-2.6 cents at C3 for the full range) and LFO speed/delay times are approximate (manual).
Pacing values are from third-party editors, not Yamaha. 70 ms per param change is conservative; Edisyn uses 50 ms.
VMEM bytes 84-127 are zero in every factory voice (DX11/V50 fields: aftertouch, effects); preserved from the last read, never edited.
The task brief called the TX81Z a half-rack: the manual gives 480 x 282 x 45.2 mm, a full-width 19-inch 1U unit, and the photos agree; the drawing is 320 x 29 like the D-110.
